title: Closed models [notes postérieures à PS ?] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: a closed model category, or a simplicial or cofibration-category context, very likely simplicial sets. X_0 -> X_1 -> ... is a sequence of cofibrations with colimit X_inf, and Y is presumably fibrant. Grothendieck studies the comparison map [X_inf, Y] -> lim_i [X_i, Y] of homotopy classes, i.e. whether homotopy classes of maps out of a sequential (homotopy) colimit are computed by the inverse limit.

(1) Surjectivity. He says this holds 'using strongly' that the X_i -> X_{i+1} are cofibrations. The standard argument: given compatible classes, choose representatives inductively. Use the homotopy extension property to replace f_{i+1} by a homotopic map whose restriction to X_i equals f_i on the nose. Then glue to a map on X_inf.

(2) Injectivity. Take f, f' : X_inf -> Y with f|X_i ~ f'|X_i for all i; one wants f ~ f'. Set B = X_inf x Delta(1) and A = X_inf u X_inf (the two ends), with A -> B a cofibration. The goal is to extend (f, f') : A -> Y to B. Filter by A_i = X_i u X_i and B_i = X_i x Delta(1). He forms the pushout B'_{i+1} = B_i u_{A_i} A_{i+1}, which is (Delta(1) x X_i) u (0 x X_{i+1}) u (1 x X_{i+1}). Its inclusion into B_{i+1} = Delta(1) x X_{i+1} is a cofibration (pushout-product). A homotopy h_i on B_i together with phi_{i+1} on A_{i+1} gives h'_{i+1} on B'_{i+1}. The problem is to extend h'_{i+1} to h_{i+1} on B_{i+1}. This is not automatic, since the cofibration is not acyclic: an arbitrary choice of h_i may obstruct the next step.

(3) Abstraction. He recasts this as a retraction problem. Given cofibrations Y -> Z_0 -> Z_1 -> ... such that each Z_i retracts onto Y, does Z_inf retract onto Y? He writes 'not clear at all'. He then correctly isolates the point: Retr(Z_i, Y) form a tower of restriction maps, which are fibrations of mapping spaces when Y is fibrant. The space Retr(Z_inf, Y) is their limit. So the question is whether lim_i pi_0 Retr(Z_i, Y) is nonempty, i.e. whether one can choose homotopy classes of retractions compatibly. For a tower of fibrations, pi_0(lim) -> lim(pi_0) is surjective, so this condition is indeed necessary and sufficient. He then writes 'Ask Ronnie Brown!'.

The neighbouring printouts are dated 06/04/82, which places the page in 1982. That is before Pursuing Stacks (Feb. 1983) and around the start of the Grothendieck–Brown contacts.
errors: The injectivity he sets out to prove is false in general. The correct statement is Milnor's exact sequence * -> lim^1 [Sigma X_i, Y] -> [X_inf, Y] -> lim [X_i, Y] -> *. Phantom maps give f not ~ 0 with all restrictions f|X_i ~ 0, e.g. maps out of CP^inf or out of skeletal filtrations of suitable CW complexes. Injectivity holds only under a Mittag-Leffler-type or lim^1 = 0 condition on [Sigma X_i, Y] (or on the relevant pi_1 of mapping spaces).

Correspondingly, the retraction question has a negative answer in general. lim of a tower of nonempty sets pi_0 Retr(Z_i, Y) can be empty because the transition maps need not be surjective. Grothendieck's 'not clear at all' is the right instinct; no proof is offered, so this is a gap rather than a stated error.
Implicit hypotheses (Y fibrant; product with Delta(1) preserving cofibrations) are not stated on the page.

ideas.what: Comparison [colim X_i, Y] -> lim [X_i, Y] for a sequence of cofibrations; surjectivity via the homotopy extension property
ideas.modern_name: Milnor lim^1 exact sequence (surjective part); homotopy classes out of a sequential homotopy colimit
ideas.usually_credited_to: J. Milnor (1962, 'On axiomatic homology theory'); Bousfield–Kan (1972) for towers of fibrations
ideas.where_published: Related discussion of homotopy limits/colimits appears in Pursuing Stacks and Les Dérivateurs, but this specific statement is unsure

ideas.what: Stepwise extension of homotopies along B_i u_{A_i} A_{i+1} -> B_{i+1} (pushout-product of a cofibration with the boundary of Delta(1))
ideas.modern_name: Pushout-product axiom / relative homotopy extension; obstruction to coherent choice of homotopies
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (Quillen 1967, homotopical algebra; earlier HEP theory)

ideas.what: Reduction to non-emptiness of lim pi_0 of a tower of retraction spaces
ideas.modern_name: pi_0(lim) -> lim pi_0 surjective for towers of fibrations; lim^1 / phantom obstruction
ideas.usually_credited_to: Bousfield–Kan (1972); Milnor (1962); phantom maps: Adams–Walker, Gray (1960s)

missed.claim: Historical detail: around 1982, apparently before Pursuing Stacks, Grothendieck was working on homotopy classes out of sequential colimits in closed model categories. He believed (or hoped) injectivity holds, did not invoke Milnor's lim^1 sequence or phantom maps, and planned to consult Ronald Brown on this point. This documents an early mathematical topic of the Grothendieck–Brown contact.
missed.quote: the whole point is to see that lim pi_0 Retr(Z_i, Y) ≠ ∅ — Ask Ronnie Brown!
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of minor interest for the chronology of Grothendieck's return to homotopy theory and his correspondence with Brown. Mathematically it is subsumed by known lim^1 theory.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is standard (Milnor lim^1 / phantom maps), and the injectivity claim pursued is false in general. Only the historical note — a 1982 homotopy-colimit question flagged 'Ask Ronnie Brown!' — is mildly interesting.
